tool_calls.name: lookup_refund_policy
tool_calls.arguments: {"query":"Can a customer request a second refund for units already refunded? What does the receipt mean and can the shop promise a bank transfer or date?"}

messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v2/payout", "title": "When the money is paid", "text": "The shop pays a refund only when all of these hold: the order qualifies, the request was on time, the units were received back and not refunded before, the order has one valid payment, the customer confirmed, a staff member approved, and the proposal is still valid. The refund is complete only when the customer has a receipt; until then nothing is reported as refunded. In this demonstration a receipt records the refund in the shop's test ledger: it is not a bank transfer, and the shop gives no date for the money to appear on a card."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/amount", "title": "Refund amount", "text": "The refund for a unit is what was paid for that unit: its price minus its share of any discount. The shares are fixed once, when the order is recorded, and never recalculated: when a paid total is split among identical units, each unit gets the total divided by the number of units, rounded down to the smallest unit of the currency, and what is left over is added one smallest unit at a time to the last units, so no unit is refunded more than its price. Shipping charges are not part of the amount. A unit for which nothing was paid has nothing to refund: a request that includes it is refused, and the other units can be requested without it. Nobody can raise the amount, so a request for more than was paid is refused with this reason."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/remaining", "title": "Each unit is refunded once", "text": "Each unit is refunded at most once, in full. A unit that was already refunded cannot be refunded again; the refund already paid is reported with its receipt. A request for more units than are left is not paid; the assistant can offer the units that remain."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}

messages.text: You’re right that the receipt is not a bank transfer. The shop’s process records refunds in its test ledger and provides no date for money to appear on a card (refund-policy/v2/payout). All three jars have already been refunded in that ledger, so they can’t be refunded again. The receipt is **R-00000001** (refund-policy/v2/remaining).
